# Cross-reference escaping probe

Every printable ASCII character except the space, each as its own level of a
cross-reference target, under `see=` and under `see-also=`. Generated to cover
the range by construction rather than by recall.

A cross-reference target is harder than an ordinary index level: it travels
through makeindex's encap channel, where an unquoted `!` is rejected outright
and Quarto turns that rejection into a failed render. A character needing a
mechanism the filter does not apply breaks this build, or is rejected by
makeindex, or fails to typeset.

Levels are written as an author must type them: a literal `!` is `!!`, a
literal `\` is `\\` and a literal `"` is `\"`, because Quarto's parser
consumes one backslash level in a quoted attribute value.

## Multi-level targets

Each character sits at a different level position under each attribute, so
leading, medial and trailing positions are all exercised across the set.

[x00]{.index see="!!!L2!L3"}
[a00]{.index see-also="L1!!!!L3"}

## Single-level targets

The special-handling set again, each alone in its target, so the typeset
cross-reference text is short enough to be compared exactly.

[Xs00]{.index see="%"}
[Xt00]{.index see-also="%"}
[Xs01]{.index see="&"}
[Xt01]{.index see-also="&"}
[Xs02]{.index see="#"}
[Xt02]{.index see-also="#"}
[Xs03]{.index see="_"}
[Xt03]{.index see-also="_"}
[Xs04]{.index see="{"}
[Xt04]{.index see-also="{"}
[Xs05]{.index see="}"}
[Xt05]{.index see-also="}"}
[Xs06]{.index see="\\"}
[Xt06]{.index see-also="\\"}
[Xs07]{.index see="~"}
[Xt07]{.index see-also="~"}
[Xs08]{.index see="^"}
[Xt08]{.index see-also="^"}
[Xs09]{.index see="$"}
[Xt09]{.index see-also="$"}
[Xs10]{.index see="@"}
[Xt10]{.index see-also="@"}
[Xs11]{.index see="|"}
[Xt11]{.index see-also="|"}
[Xs12]{.index see="!!"}
[Xt12]{.index see-also="!!"}
[Xs13]{.index see="\""}
[Xt13]{.index see-also="\""}
[Xs14]{.index see="<"}
[Xt14]{.index see-also="<"}
[Xs15]{.index see=">"}
[Xt15]{.index see-also=">"}

## Both attributes on one mark

The dual-target form, which emits one command carrying both targets.

[Xb00]{.index see="%" see-also="%"}
[Xb01]{.index see="&" see-also="&"}
[Xb02]{.index see="#" see-also="#"}
[Xb03]{.index see="_" see-also="_"}
[Xb04]{.index see="{" see-also="{"}
[Xb05]{.index see="}" see-also="}"}
[Xb06]{.index see="\\" see-also="\\"}
[Xb07]{.index see="~" see-also="~"}
[Xb08]{.index see="^" see-also="^"}
[Xb09]{.index see="$" see-also="$"}
[Xb10]{.index see="@" see-also="@"}
[Xb11]{.index see="|" see-also="|"}
[Xb12]{.index see="!!" see-also="!!"}
[Xb13]{.index see="\"" see-also="\""}
[Xb14]{.index see="<" see-also="<"}
[Xb15]{.index see=">" see-also=">"}

## Targets that cannot be used

A target with an empty level drops that level and warns; a target with nothing
usable in it leaves the mark indexed without a cross-reference, and warns.

[Xe00]{.index see="A!"}
[Xe01]{.index see=""}
